manifest.name: dsh-hydrasearch
manifest.description: TinyFish + AnySearch web search and fetch provider for DeepSeek Harness (DSH): registers a ctx.web failover chain with an operator-controlled backend priority, so the built-in web_search and web_fetch tools run through TinyFish and AnySearch, with a settings card in the Plugins page.
manifest.author: dgagf111

scripts.verify:all: node scripts/verify.mjs && node scripts/verify-client.mjs && node scripts/verify-e2e.mjs && node scripts/verify-workflow.mjs && node scripts/verify-profile.mjs && node scripts/verify-integration.mjs

bundle.text:
# dsh-hydrasearch — TinyFish + AnySearch web search and fetch for DeepSeek Harness.
#
# This file is the package's Bundle patch. The profile loader composes it (see
# `dsh.profile.bundles` in the profile's package.json) BEFORE the profile's own
# cordis.patch.yml, so the user layer always wins on conflict.
#
# TARGETS DSH 0.2.0-rc.2 ONLY. The `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` peer ranges in
# package.json are the enforced contract, not `dsh.engines.dsh` (declarative) or
# `dsh.compatibility.dshReleases` (read by nothing): app-boot checks every
# `@deepseek-ai/dsh*` peer range with `semver.satisfies(runtimeVersion, range,
# { includePrerelease: true })`, and a bundle that fails is skipped ENTIRELY
# before this file is ever read — no row, no card, no error in the UI. Bumping
# the peers is therefore part of every DSH upgrade, not a formality.
#
# The row id below (`hydrasearch`) is load-bearing: the browser half registers
# its Plugins-page configuration page under the slot key
# `<package name>#<row id>` = `dsh-hydrasearch#hydrasearch`
# (see ui-plugin-manager rowConfigKey). Renaming the id without updating
# lib/client.js silently removes the configuration page from the Plugins page.
#
# WHY `name` IS `./lib/index.js` — RELATIVE TO **THIS FILE**, NOT TO THE PROFILE
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Two things are true at once, and getting either wrong makes the row report
# "failed to import" (`entry.fiber === undefined`):
#
# 1. A BARE specifier cannot work. The packaged desktop app's Loader lives inside
#    `app.asar`, OUTSIDE the profile tree, so `dsh-hydrasearch` resolves from the
#    app's own installation and never reaches `<profile>/node_modules`.
#
# 2. A relative name is anchored by `app-boot`'s `anchorInsertedPluginNames()`
#    against THE DIRECTORY OF THE PATCH FILE THAT DECLARED IT — not against the
#    profile root. `loadOverlayPatches()` rewrites every `./…` / `../…` insert
#    name to `pathToFileURL(resolve(dirname(patchFile), name))`.
#
# This file lives in the package directory itself
# (`<profile>/node_modules/dsh-hydrasearch/`), so the entry is `./lib/index.js`.
#
# The previous value, `./node_modules/dsh-hydrasearch/lib/index.js`, assumed
# profile-root anchoring. Under (2) it anchored to the PACKAGE directory and
# double-nested into
#   <profile>/node_modules/dsh-hydrasearch/node_modules/dsh-hydrasearch/lib/index.js
# which does not exist — and that is literally the "failed to import" path the
# desktop app prints in its banner.
#
# Consequence: this layer's convention is the OPPOSITE of the profile's own
# `cordis.patch.yml`, which resolves `./plugins/…` against the profile root. That
# works only because that file itself sits in the profile root. Same rule, two
# different results — never copy a path from one layer into the other.
#
# Installing as a BUNDLE is still required and still correct: it is what makes
# the package appear on the Plugins page and dispatch `plugins.row.config`.
# The two requirements are independent — bundle membership for VISIBILITY, a
# path for LOADABILITY.
#
# Config keys not listed here inherit the schema defaults in lib/index.js. Every
# value below is editable from the card: on 0.2.0-rc.2 a settings write goes
# through `settings.mutate()` into THIS row's `config` inside the profile's own
# `cordis.patch.yml`, so an edit survives a restart and can be reviewed as a diff.
#
# `web.searchProvider` / `web.fetchProvider` are deliberately NOT set here: the
# plugin claims an unset seat at apply() time, and a row config REPLACES the
# whole `web` config, so setting only one id would silently drop the other (the
# same trap dsh-free-search's patch documents). Configure both or neither.
- insert:
    - id: hydrasearch
      name: ./lib/index.js
      config:
        # Ordered backend ids; earlier wins. Reorder by dragging in the card.
        priority:
          - tinyfish
          - anysearch
        # Walk the chain when a backend fails. Off = first available backend is final.
        failover: true
        takeOverSearch: true
        takeOverFetch: true
        # 'auto' follows `priority`; otherwise pin one backend id.
        # Pinning is config-only: the plugin registers a single provider, so
        # these two selectors are how you bypass the chain.
        searchBackend: auto
        fetchBackend: auto

        tinyfish:
          enabled: true
          # The API key is NOT configured here. It lives ONLY in the credential
          # center, under the plugin-owned ref HYDRASEARCH_TINYFISH_API_KEY,
          # written from the settings card. Environment variables are not read.
          searchBaseURL: https://api.search.tinyfish.ai/
          fetchBaseURL: https://api.fetch.tinyfish.ai/
          # Non-empty by default: the "why" behind the request, sent as `purpose`
          # on BOTH the search and fetch path. Blank it to send no purpose.
          purpose: Gather current, citable web sources to answer a user question
          language: ''
          location: ''
          # web | news | research_paper; blank lets the service decide.
          domainType: ''
          includeDomains: ''
          excludeDomains: ''
          # YYYY-MM-DD bounds; blank disables.
          afterDate: ''
          beforeDate: ''
          # Freshness window in minutes, publication-year bounds; 0 disables.
          recencyMinutes: 0
          pubYearMin: 0
          pubYearMax: 0
          # Pages per search (1-10); each page is one billed round trip.
          maxPages: 3
          # markdown | html | json
          fetchFormat: markdown
          fetchLinks: false
          fetchImageLinks: false
          # Per-URL fetch budget in ms; 0 omits it (service accepts 1-110000).
          fetchPerUrlTimeoutMs: 0
          # Fetch cache tolerance in seconds. -1 omits `ttl` (accept any cached
          # entry), 0 forces a live fetch, N accepts cache younger than N seconds.
          fetchTtlSeconds: -1
          verbose: false

        anysearch:
          enabled: true
          # As with tinyfish: the key lives only in the credential center, under
          # HYDRASEARCH_ANYSEARCH_API_KEY. An empty key is legal — AnySearch
          # allows anonymous access at a lower quota.
          # Empty uses $ANYSEARCH_API_BASE_URL, then the public host.
          baseURL: ''
          # Vertical sub-domain tag (e.g. finance.quote); blank = general web search.
          tag: ''
          # Vertical parameters as a JSON object string; requires `tag`.
          params: ''
          zone: ''
          language: ''
          # 1-10
          maxResults: 10
          verbose: false

readme.text: [English](./README.en.md) | **中文**

给 DeepSeek Harness 加上两个免费、几乎不限量的网页搜索后端。

装好之后，DSH 内置的 `web_search` / `web_fetch` 背后就多了一层保障：TinyFish 与 AnySearch 两个后端轮流待命，一个不行自动换另一个。

> **当前版本 0.4.0，已支持 DSH 0.2.0-rc.2。** 已在本机 0.2.0-rc.2 桌面版实测：插件正常加载，`web_search` 与 `web_fetch` 都通过 TinyFish / AnySearch 链路返回结果。旧版本（0.1.x-rc.6、0.1.6-alpha.2、0.1.7-alpha.1、0.1.7-rc.1）已不再支持，原因见「支持的 DSH 版本」。

- **都免费，频率限制极高。** TinyFish 与 AnySearch 都提供免费额度，日常搜索与抓取基本用不完。AnySearch 甚至不必先申请 key，匿名即可使用（只是额度低一些）。
- **双后端自动故障切换。** 某个后端超时、限流或出错，自动切到下一个，搜索不会因为一个后端的问题而整体失败。

| 后端 | 费用 | 限流 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TinyFish 搜索 | 免费，不消耗账户余额 | 30 次/分钟 · 500 次/小时 |
| TinyFish 抓取 | 免费，不消耗账户余额 | 150 个网址/分钟 · 1000 个网址/天 |
| AnySearch（已填 key） | 免费档 1000 次/天 | 20 QPS |
| AnySearch（匿名） | 共用每日免费额度 | 按客户端 IP 限流，低于上者 |

TinyFish 的搜索与抓取在任何账户余额下都免费，余额为 0 也照常工作。AnySearch 不填 key 也能用，填 key 后升到免费档。数据来自两家官网，可能调整，以官网为准。

- **搜索**：网页搜索，可按语言、地区、时间范围、站点黑白名单、垂直领域筛选，并控制每次翻几页。
- **抓取**：把指定网址抓成 Markdown、HTML 或 JSON，可选同时带出页面内的链接与图片链接。

一条命令添加本仓库，然后重启 DSH：`dsh plugin --profile web add github:dgagf111/dsh-hydrasearch`

重启后打开 **插件页 → 已安装 → `dsh-hydrasearch` → 行内配置入口**。首次使用需要在卡片里给 TinyFish 填一个 key；AnySearch 可以先不填。

> 装好后可直接用 DSH 的 `web_search` / `web_fetch` 验证：两者都应正常返回，说明请求确实走了 TinyFish / AnySearch 链路，而不是内置的官方搜索。

| DSH 版本 | 状态 |
| --- | --- |
| **0.2.0-rc.2** | ✅ **已支持** — peerDependencies 声明为 `^0.2.0-rc.2`，`manifestVersion` 为 1，`dsh.engines.dsh` 为 `>=0.2.0-rc.2`；已在本机桌面版实测通过 |
| 0.1.6-alpha.2 / 0.1.7-alpha.1 / 0.1.7-rc.1 / 0.1.x-rc.6 | ❌ 不再支持（有意放弃，非遗漏） |

旧代际为什么放弃：DSH 会按插件的 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` peer 范围做一次兼容性闸门检查，**只要有一个 peer 范围不满足，整个 bundle 会被直接跳过**——插件不会出现在「已安装」列表里（连灰色不可用的一行都没有），界面上也没有任何提示，唯一的痕迹是启动时 stderr 上的一行 `skipping profile bundle "dsh-hydrasearch": ... is incompatible with dsh 0.2.0-rc.2`。旧版本的 peer 是 `^0.1.0-rc.6`，在 0.2.0-rc.2 上不满足，于是整包消失；0.4.0 把 peer 提到 `^0.2.0-rc.2` 即修复。

1. 升级 DSH 到 0.2.0-rc.2。
2. 重跑安装命令，让 profile 拿到 0.4.0：`dsh plugin --profile web add github:dgagf111/dsh-hydrasearch`（`dsh plugin` 只是把你给的参数转发给 profile 目录里的 pnpm 并重新对齐 bundle 列表，所以这个命令重复执行是安全的）。
3. 重启 DSH。

**API key 需要重新填写一次。** 0.3.0 起凭据引用改成了插件自有命名（`HYDRASEARCH_TINYFISH_API_KEY` / `HYDRASEARCH_ANYSEARCH_API_KEY`）——旧名字会被常见的环境变量名遮蔽，导致卡片能存不能改、能存不能清。旧引用下的 key 不会被读取，请在卡片里重新填入。

本版本变更的完整说明见 [CHANGELOG.md](./CHANGELOG.md)，机制层面的记录见 [docs/](./docs/)。

全部在插件页的 `dsh-hydrasearch` 卡片里完成：

- **后端顺序**：拖动调整，排在前面的先用。
- **故障切换**：默认开启；关闭后只使用第一个可用的后端，它的失败就是最终结果。
- **后端参数**：搜索地址、语言、地区、时间范围、站点过滤、翻页数、抓取格式、超时、缓存策略等，按需填写，留空即不发送。

- **key 只存在你自己机器上的凭据中心**（DSH 的本地凭据文件），不上传、不同步、不写进日志。
- 插件只把 key 放进请求头，发给**你所调用的那个搜索服务本身**，除此之外没有任何第三方接收方；插件自身也不包含遥测或使用统计上报。
- 读取、写入、清除三个动作指向同一个存储位置。

**English** | [中文](./README.md)

Two free, barely-rate-limited web search backends for DeepSeek Harness.

Once installed, the built-in `web_search` / `web_fetch` gain a safety net: TinyFish and AnySearch stand by in order, and one takes over automatically when the other fails.

> **Version 0.4.0, and DSH 0.2.0-rc.2 is supported.** Verified on a local 0.2.0-rc.2 desktop build: the plugin loads, and both `web_search` and `web_fetch` return through the TinyFish / AnySearch chain. The older generations (0.1.x-rc.6, 0.1.6-alpha.2, 0.1.7-alpha.1, 0.1.7-rc.1) are no longer supported — see "Supported DSH versions".

- **Both are free, with very high rate limits.** TinyFish and AnySearch both offer free usage that everyday searching and fetching will not exhaust. AnySearch does not even require a key up front — anonymous access works, at a lower quota.
- **Automatic failover between two backends.** If one times out, gets rate-limited, or errors out, the next one takes over, so a search never fails as a whole because of a single backend.

| Backend | Cost | Rate limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TinyFish Search | Free, never draws from your balance | 30 requests/min · 500 requests/hour |
| TinyFish Fetch | Free, never draws from your balance | 150 URLs/min · 1,000 URLs/day |
| AnySearch (with key) | Free tier: 1,000 requests/day | 20 QPS |
| AnySearch (anonymous) | Shares the daily free quota | Rate-limited per client IP, lower than the above |

TinyFish Search and Fetch are free at any account balance and keep working at $0. AnySearch works without a key too, and a key raises it to the free tier. Figures come from the vendors' sites and may change; the official pages are authoritative.

- **Search**: web search with language, region, date range, site allow/deny lists, and vertical-domain filters, plus control over how many pages each search may fetch.
- **Fetch**: turn a given URL into Markdown, HTML, or JSON, optionally returning the page's links and image links too.

Add this repository with one command, then restart DSH: `dsh plugin --profile web add github:dgagf111/dsh-hydrasearch`

After the restart, open **Plugins page → Installed → `dsh-hydrasearch` → the row's configure entry**. On first use, enter a TinyFish key in the card; AnySearch can be left without one.

> To check it works, just use DSH's `web_search` / `web_fetch`: both should return normally, which means the request really went through the TinyFish / AnySearch chain rather than the built-in official search.

| DSH version | Status |
| --- | --- |
| **0.2.0-rc.2** | ✅ **Supported** — peerDependencies are `^0.2.0-rc.2`, `manifestVersion` is 1, `dsh.engines.dsh` is `>=0.2.0-rc.2`; verified on a local desktop build |
| 0.1.6-alpha.2 / 0.1.7-alpha.1 / 0.1.7-rc.1 / 0.1.x-rc.6 | ❌ No longer supported (dropped deliberately, not by omission) |

Why the older generations were dropped: DSH runs a compatibility gate over a plugin's `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` peer ranges, and if any range is unsatisfied the **entire bundle is skipped** — it does not appear in the Installed list at all (not even as a greyed-out row) and the UI says nothing; the one trace is a stderr line at startup, `skipping profile bundle "dsh-hydrasearch": ... is incompatible with dsh 0.2.0-rc.2`. The old peers were `^0.1.0-rc.6`, which `0.2.0-rc.2` does not satisfy, so the whole package vanished; raising the peers to `^0.2.0-rc.2` in 0.4.0 is the fix.

1. Update DSH to 0.2.0-rc.2.
2. Re-run the install command so the profile picks up 0.4.0: `dsh plugin --profile web add github:dgagf111/dsh-hydrasearch` (`dsh plugin` forwards its arguments to pnpm inside the profile and then re-reconciles the bundle list, so running it again is safe).
3. Restart DSH.

**Re-enter your API key once.** Since 0.3.0 the credential references are plugin-owned (`HYDRASEARCH_TINYFISH_API_KEY` / `HYDRASEARCH_ANYSEARCH_API_KEY`) — the old names collided with conventional environment variables, which made a stored key impossible to replace or clear. A key stored under the old reference is not read any more; enter it again in the card.

See [CHANGELOG.md](./CHANGELOG.md) for the full list of changes in this release, and [docs/](./docs/) for the mechanism-level notes.

Everything happens in the `dsh-hydrasearch` card on the Plugins page:

- **Backend order**: drag to reorder; the topmost backend is tried first.
- **Failover**: on by default; turn it off and only the first available backend is used, whose failure is final.
- **Backend parameters**: search endpoint, language, region, date range, site filters, page count, fetch format, timeout, cache policy and more — fill in what you need, leave the rest blank to omit them.

- **The key lives only in the credential center on your own machine** (DSH's local credentials file). It is never uploaded, never synced, and never written to logs.
- The plugin places the key in the request header sent to **the search service you are calling**, and to nothing else. There is no other recipient, and the plugin itself contains no telemetry or usage reporting.
- Read, write, and clear all target that same store.
